question: With every stage merged and installed, what does a gesture actually cost, and what breaks?

setup.device: DAYU200 development board, 720x1280, display powered on
setup.foregroundApp: com.ohos.settings (a neutral screen, set by the maintainer)
daemon: The installed helper was rebuilt from main at #1512 and re-signed with the
maintainer's own Developer ID (8AQTYW5FKR), same identifier, hardened runtime
and entitlements as the build it replaced. Previous bundle kept under
setup.clientPath: the arkdeck CLI, which spawns a process and opens a socket per invocation. CORRECTED: this file previously said the App holds a live connection and does not pay that cost. The App opens a fresh NSXPCConnection per request and invalidates it afterwards, and the two paths measure within ~25ms of each other. See app-path-verification.json.

sessionCarriedEvidence: First gesture of a session ran all three preamble steps.
with the journal recording `read-evidence-model carried from session readback at ...`
and the same for firmware. #1510 confirmed live.
capabilityUseLedger: `runtime-capabilities.ledger` appeared on first use and grew 1.3k -> 7.1k while
the 1.3 MB document was left untouched. #1511 confirmed live - and the document
being 1.3 MB is what the old shape rewrote twice per gesture.
persistentChannel: `ps` showed a long-lived `hdc -t <key> shell` whose parent is the daemon.

reading: p50 through the CLI is 644ms. Subtracting the CLI's own startup and XPC round
trips brings the App's path lower, but the App path was not measured and no
p95 is the honest problem: under sustained tapping the same gesture ranged from
636ms to 11820ms. The 400ms gate is not met end to end.

theTail: SUPERSEDED - see supersededBy. Kept for the record, not as a current conclusion.
A 24-gesture batch degraded progressively (1.0s -> 11.8s) and then recovered.
Measured at rest immediately after: `hdc list targets -v` p50 40ms with no missing
rows, `uinput` p50 313ms spawned, device loadavg 2.10 (this board's baseline).
So the tail is the device and its link under sustained gesture load, not the
Runtime - but it is real, and it is what stands between these components and the
gate. Characterising it is not done.

twoFailuresWhichWereNotDefects.reason: targetConfirmationMismatch: expected exactly one matching target row, saw 0
reading: The device dropped off the hdc target list momentarily under load. Both jobs
failed at `confirm-evidence-target`, before anything was injected, with
This is the per-gesture identity re-confirmation kept in #1510 doing exactly what
it is for: it refused to inject into a target it could not confirm. The cheapest
step in the preamble is the one that caught a real transient.

defectFoundAndFixed.claim: an open channel closes after 120s without a gesture
defectFoundAndFixed.observed: still open 11 minutes after the last gesture
cause: The idle sweep ran only from `dispatch`, so it could only close a channel when
another gesture arrived - which is precisely not the case it exists for. The
claim was false as implemented, in the commit message and in this evidence set.
defectFoundAndFixed.fix: the sweep is armed on a timer and re-armed on every use, so it measures from the last gesture
defectFoundAndFixed.test: testAnIdleChannelClosesWithoutWaitingForAnotherGesture; with the arming removed it fails

verifiedOnHardwareAfterTheFix.daemon: rebuilt from main at #1513 and re-signed with the maintainer's Developer ID; previous bundle kept under Helpers/.backup-20260825T213042/
verifiedOnHardwareAfterTheFix.opened: one gesture opened a channel owned by the daemon (pid parented to it)
verifiedOnHardwareAfterTheFix.closedAfterIdleSeconds: between 105 and 120, sampled every 15s with nothing dispatched; the channel's own elapsed time read 2:01 at the last sample before it disappeared
verifiedOnHardwareAfterTheFix.reopened: the next gesture opened a fresh channel; five gestures then ran at 520-653ms with only ['confirm-evidence-target', 'inject-pointer-input'] reaching the device

notVerified: The App's own path. Everything here went through the CLI.
The p95 tail under sustained gesture load, which is what stands between the
component measurements and the 400ms gate. It is device-and-link side, not
Runtime, and it is not characterised.

what: The tail figures in this file (p95 3887ms, and the 7141/18834ms runs) were
measured on the daemon carrying the idle-close defect. They do not reproduce on
the build that fixes it: 100 consecutive gestures ran at p50 544ms, p95 569ms,
The reading in `theTail` - that the tail is device-and-link side rather than
Runtime - was drawn from phases run sequentially rather than interleaved, and
did not survive interleaving. Do not carry it forward.
